headline: AI agents are changing startup hiring strategies, discussed at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
summary: AI agents are taking on roles in engineering, customer support, and operations, forcing founders to rethink traditional hiring. This shift will be a key topic at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.
details: AI agents are increasingly performing roles like engineering, customer support, and operations in startups. This trend challenges founders to decide what work should be delegated to AI versus human employees. The topic will be explored at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.

The session, titled "Hiring When AI Is a Co-Founder," will feature Josh Reeves (Gusto CEO), Michelle Johnson (Insight Partners SVP), and John Koelliker (Leland CEO). They will discuss how early-stage companies integrate humans and AI agents without sacrificing speed or culture.

For startups, every hire involves trade-offs in capability, cost, and speed. AI agents introduce a new option, allowing small teams to move faster by delegating multistep tasks. This prompts a fundamental shift from "Who do we hire?" to "What work needs to be done, and is a person the best way?"

Delegating to AI agents raises new questions about ownership, accountability, and error handling. Founders must consider which responsibilities are too critical to delegate. These are no longer theoretical questions for companies building AI-native startups.

Josh Reeves of Gusto, which supports over 500,000 companies, offers a broad perspective on this shift. Gusto combines AI with a decade of experience in HR and payroll, giving insight into how businesses are adapting their team growth strategies.

Michelle Johnson from Insight Partners will discuss startup scaling, focusing on go-to-market strategy and AI implementation. She will explore how AI agents in sales processes change the skills startups prioritize when hiring.

John Koelliker, CEO of Leland, a talent platform for the AI era, brings expertise in how people develop and apply skills in a changing labor market. His insights will cover the intersection of talent and AI.
The panel will collectively address how to design startup teams when AI agents can contribute from day one. Attendees can learn more at Moscone West in San Francisco, October 13–15, 2026.

headline_marked: [[Signing keys for US driver's license barcodes recovered]] in security research
headline: Signing keys for US driver's license barcodes recovered in security research
summary: Security researchers have successfully recovered the signing keys used for US driver's license barcodes, highlighting a potential vulnerability in the system.
details: A security researcher has successfully recovered the signing keys used for US driver's license barcodes. This significant discovery was detailed on a personal website, highlighting a potential vulnerability in the system.

These signing keys are crucial for verifying the authenticity of the 2D barcodes found on driver's licenses. Their recovery means that it could theoretically be possible to forge or manipulate these barcodes, potentially impacting identity verification processes.

The research underscores the importance of robust cryptographic practices and regular security audits for government-issued identification. It prompts a re-evaluation of the security measures protecting sensitive personal data embedded in physical documents.

The researcher's work, published on their personal blog, serves as a proof-of-concept for the vulnerability. It aims to inform authorities and the public about the risks associated with current barcode implementations.
